proposed_survivor_patch.title: Ivanka Trump’s Company Receives Three Provisional Chinese Trademark Approvals on April 6, 2017
proposed_survivor_patch.description_short: China provisionally approved three trademarks for Ivanka Trump’s company on April 6, 2017, the day she dined with Xi Jinping.
proposed_survivor_patch.description_medium: China provisionally approved three trademarks for Ivanka Trump’s company on April 6, 2017, the day she and Jared Kushner dined with Xi Jinping at Mar-a-Lago. CNN said the marks covered jewelry, spa services and bags. Its report said 16 marks were already fully registered; three, not 16, received preliminary approval that day.
proposed_survivor_patch.description_long: On April 6, 2017, Chinese authorities granted preliminary approval to three trademark applications from Ivanka Trump’s company. AP reported they were 2016 applications and that approvals coincided with Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner dining with Xi Jinping and his wife at Mar-a-Lago. CNN identified the marks as covering jewelry, spa services and bags, based on Chinese trademark documents it reviewed. The 16 in the original title referred to marks CNN said the company already held as fully registered; it was not the number newly approved on April 6. CNN’s story was published April 18, while AP’s follow-up appeared April 19, so April 18 is a report date rather than the approval date. These sources establish timing and provisional approvals, but do not show that Trump or Ivanka Trump intervened in the process, that the dinner caused the approvals, or that the grants were improper. A Chinese foreign ministry spokesman said applications were handled lawfully and fairly. This copy preserves the documented timing and corrects the count while keeping any conflict concern separate from proof of a trade or policy favor.
